Cell purity. Let $z$ be a central idempotent of $A$. On the cell layer $J_\lambda\cong C_\lambda^*\otimes_FC_\lambda$ the equality of left and right multiplication by $z$ gives $B\otimes\operatorname{Id}=\operatorname{Id}\otimes A_\lambda$ for the first- and second-factor coefficient matrices; comparing matrix coefficients shows every off-diagonal entry of $B$ and $A_\lambda$ vanishes and all diagonal entries of $B$ and $A_\lambda$ are equal, so both are a single scalar $\theta_\lambda$ times the identity. Applying this to all primitive central idempotents, whose sum is $1$, exactly one acts as $1$ on the nonzero cell module $C_\lambda$ and the others as $0$; hence $C_\lambda$, and therefore every composition factor of it, lies in one block. and $s_{i,j}=0$ if $i\ge j$, together with the centralizer elements
$$e_{i,j;r}=\sum_{\substack{\mathrm{row}(h)=i,\ \mathrm{row}(k)=j\\ \mathrm{col}(k)-\mathrm{col}(h)=r}}e_{h,k} \qquad(s_{i,j}\le r<p_j).$$

The $e_{i,j;r}$ are linearly independent because they are sums over pairwise disjoint matrix units, and their number is $\sum_{i,j}\#\{r:s_{i,j}\le r<p_j\}=\sum_{i,j}(p_j-\max(0,p_j-p_i))=\sum_{i,j}\min(p_i,p_j)$, which equals $\dim\mathfrak g^e$ by [F2]. Hence they form a basis of $\mathfrak g^e$.

The bijection $J\to K$. For $(a,b)\in J$ put $i=\mathrm{row}(a)$, $j=\mathrm{row}(b)$ and $r=\mathrm{col}(b)-\mathrm{col}(a)$. Because $b$ is rightmost, $\mathrm{col}(b)=p_j$; hence $r=p_j-\mathrm{col}(a)\ge0$, $r<p_j$ because $\mathrm{col}(a)\ge1$, and $r\ge p_j-p_i$ because $\mathrm{col}(a)\le p_i$. Thus $s_{i,j}=\max(0,p_j-p_i)\le r<p_j$, so the map lands in $K$. The triple determines $b$ as the rightmost box of row $j$ and $a$ as the box of row $i$ in column $p_j-r$, proving injectivity. Conversely, if $(i,j,r)\in K$, then $r<p_j$ gives $1\le p_j-r$, while $r\ge\max(0,p_j-p_i)$ gives $p_j-r\le p_i$. Thus those two boxes exist, their columns satisfy $\mathrm{col}(a)\le\mathrm{col}(b)$, and they give the required preimage. If either row has length zero, the index range in $K$ is empty, consistently with the absence of such a box pair.

For $x,y\in\mathfrak m$ one has $[x,y]\in[\mathfrak m,\mathfrak m]\subseteq\mathfrak g_{\le-2}$ by step 1.2, and $e\in\mathfrak g_1$, so $[x,y]e\in\mathfrak g_{\le-1}$ and $\operatorname{tr}([x,y]e)=0$ by [F3]. Hence $\chi([\mathfrak m,\mathfrak m])=0$, that is, $\chi$ is a Lie algebra character on $\mathfrak m$: for $x,y\in\mathfrak m$, $\chi([x,y])=\operatorname{tr}([x,y]e)=0$.

The good-grading conditions. By step 1.3, the centralizer $\mathfrak g^e$ has a homogeneous basis $e_{i,j;r}$ with $r\ge s_{i,j}\ge0$, so it has no negative-degree part. Invariance gives $\operatorname{tr}([e,x]y)=-\operatorname{tr}(x[e,y])$, so the transpose of the map on degree $r$ is, up to sign, $\operatorname{ad}e:\mathfrak g_{-r-1}\to\mathfrak g_{-r}$. At the last link the available number of $a$ letters is $m$ and its $a$-diagram must be dominated by $\eta'$, since its powers factor through the shorter chain. ([[def-classical-complex-matrix-lie-algebras]]), and let
$\partial X=X\setminus\mathrm{GL}(V)\cdot e$. Then $\mathbb C[X]$ is a reduced
irreducible normal domain and $\operatorname{codim}_X\partial X\ge2$. This
holds for every Jordan type, not only the regular nilpotent cone.

$B_1A_1=0$, $B_iA_i=A_{i-1}B_{i-1}$ $(2\le i<t)$. Then $Z$ is a complete
intersection, smooth outside a closed subset of codimension $\ge2$, reduced,
irreducible and normal, and the invariant ring $\mathbb C[Z]^H$ under
$H=\prod_{i<t}\mathrm{GL}(U_i)$ is the coordinate ring of $X$ via the end map

([[def-commuting-symmetric-and-linear-actions-on-tensor-power]]). Let $A$ be

extending the place action, and let
$B:=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}\{g^{\otimes n}:g\in\operatorname{GL}(V)\}$
be the linear span of the diagonal operators
$g^{\otimes n}(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n)=gv_1\otimes\cdots\otimes gv_n$.

  $A\in M_{2n}(\mathbb C)$ with $AJ+JA^{T}=0$, for $n\ge1$, where
  $J=\begin{pmatrix}0&I_n\\-I_n&0\end{pmatrix}$.

  $\mathfrak{so}_{2n+1}(\mathbb C)$ are the sets of $A\in M_m(\mathbb C)$ with
  $AJ+JA^{T}=0$, for $n\ge1$, where $J=\begin{pmatrix}0&I_n\\I_n&0\end{pmatrix}$ for

Let $A=\mathbb C[X]$ and let $f\in\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ be regular on $O$, hence regular off a closed subset of $X\setminus O$; since $\partial X$ has codimension $\ge2$ in $X$ by the normality lemma [F1], $f$ is regular in codimension $1$ and therefore extends to $A$ by [F2]. Applying this coordinatewise to maps into a finite-dimensional vector space shows that every regular map $O\to W$ into a finite-dimensional vector space extends uniquely to a regular map $X\to W$.

The equivariant map on $O$. Fix $B\in\operatorname{End}(V^{\otimes d})^{G_e}$ and define, for $g\in\mathrm{GL}(V)$, $F(g\,e\,g^{-1}):=(g^{\otimes d})\,B\,(g^{-1})^{\otimes d}\in\operatorname{End}(V^{\otimes d})$. This is well defined: if $g_1e g_1^{-1}=g_2eg_2^{-1}$, then $g_2^{-1}g_1\in G_e$, so $(g_2^{-1}g_1)^{\otimes d}B(g_2^{-1}g_1)^{-\otimes d}=B$ by $G_e$-invariance, which rearranges to $(g_1^{\otimes d})B(g_1^{-1})^{\otimes d}=(g_2^{\otimes d})B(g_2^{-1})^{\otimes d}$. The map $F$ is $\mathrm{GL}(V)$-equivariant by construction: $F(hXh^{-1})=(h^{\otimes d})F(X)(h^{-1})^{\otimes d}$ for $X\in O$.

Regularity of $F$ on $O$. The ranks of $X^0,X^1,\dots,X^{l-1}$ are constant on $O$. Cover $O$ by open charts where fixed minors used to select bases of the kernels and images, their quotient complements and Jordan top vectors are nonzero. Gaussian elimination on such a chart gives a Jordan basis for $X$ with entries regular in $X$. Let $g(X)$ carry a fixed Jordan basis for $e$ to this chosen Jordan basis for $X$, with the same ordered string lengths. Then $g(X)e g(X)^{-1}=X$. Restricting to the open chart where the Jordan-basis determinant is nonzero makes both $g(X)$ and $g(X)^{-1}$ regular, since their entries have only the fixed nonvanishing minors and determinant as denominators. Thus $X\mapsto(g(X)^{\otimes d})B(g(X)^{-1})^{\otimes d}$ is the map of step 1.2 and is regular on each chart. These charts cover $O$; on overlaps $g_2(X)^{-1}g_1(X)\in G_e$, so the expressions agree by $G_e$-invariance of $B$. Hence $F$ is regular on $O$.

Extension to $X$. By steps 1.2 and 2.1 the map $F\colon O\to\operatorname{End}(V^{\otimes d})$ is a regular equivariant map on the dense orbit; by step 1.1 it extends uniquely to a regular map $F\colon X\to\operatorname{End}(V^{\otimes d})$. Since $\mathbb C[X]=\mathbb C[\operatorname{End}(V)]/I(X)$ and $X$ is an affine closed subset of the affine space $\operatorname{End}(V)$, the coordinate functions of $F$ are restrictions of polynomial functions on $\operatorname{End}(V)$; fixing representatives gives a polynomial map $\Phi\colon\operatorname{End}(V)\to\operatorname{End}(V^{\otimes d})$ extending $F$.

Equivariance of $\Phi$. For fixed $g\in\mathrm{GL}(V)$, both sides of $\Phi(gXg^{-1})=(g^{\otimes d})\Phi(X)(g^{-1})^{\otimes d}$ are polynomial maps in $X$; they agree on the dense orbit $O$ by step 1.2 and hence on all of $X$. Consequently the class of $\Phi$ in the finite-dimensional space of polynomial maps $\operatorname{End}(V)\to\operatorname{End}(V^{\otimes d})$ of degree at most $K$ (for $K$ at least the degree of $\Phi$), modulo the $\mathrm{GL}(V)$-stable subspace of maps vanishing on $X$, is invariant for the conjugation action. By the invariant-lifting property of complete reducibility [F3], this class has an invariant representative $\Phi'$ of degree at most $K$; then $\Phi'$ is a $\mathrm{GL}(V)$-equivariant polynomial map on $\operatorname{End}(V)$ agreeing with $F$ on $X$, and $\Phi'(e)=F(e)=B$ since $e\in O$, which is assertion (1).
